nesnd_external_hus_desc: News of the Southern succession has reached Dongzhou. The Zheng maritime empire we once fought for our independence is now split over who should rule it. Zheng's enemies may come to the republic for help, and the merchants are watching what becomes of the ports and sea lanes.\n\nIt is a chance to widen our ties abroad. But every subsidy we send abroad comes out of the republic's own treasury and factories.
nesnd_external_fra_desc: Southern envoys ask France to recognise the new dynasty and honour the old treaties. In India, the quarrel over the southern coast and the colonies is still unsettled. French merchants, creditors and officers have money riding on both.
nesnd_external_qe1_desc: Caravans from Sichuan have brought news of the Southern dispute. After the defeat at Dunhuang, Western Qin cannot afford to squander men or money again. If war returns to the east, the Bashu roads will strain under trade and frontier defence at once.
nesnd_external_sha_desc: News of the Southern succession has reached the northern republic. Exiles have spotted old names in the war reports, and some are already writing to comrades in Dongzhou. Old friendships like these might yet buy the republic money and guns.
nesnd_external_bur_desc: The Southern succession will change how the court deals with its powerful neighbour. Neither the river trade nor the duties of the old treaties can be set aside. Before promising money or arms to anyone, the court must work out who can be trusted.
nesnd_external_mug_desc: The Southern succession has reopened old accounts on the Indian coast. Ming holdings in Mysore and their coastal trading rights have long been a thorn in the empire's side. Our ministers can ask France for money and arms, and if the Southern court still holds land in Mysore, now is the moment to press our claim.
nesnd_external_gbr_desc: While France and Ming stood together, British shipping was hemmed in on every route. Now the Southern succession is contested: merchants hope to slip into new ports, and London is free to choose its friends again.
nesnd_external_rus_desc: Russia's eastern frontier is long, and the Southern dispute touches St Petersburg's interests too. A dependable trading partner, or a government willing to take our aid, would make Russia's position in the east easier. We can wait until the victor is clear, or spend money and arms now, while every side is still looking for friends.
nesnd_external_policy_reason: The Southern succession has thrown old treaties, trade routes and the fate of overseas dependencies into doubt. Envoys are on the move: some come asking for help, others wait for us to speak first. Treaties already signed still bind those who signed them.
nesnd_external_arms_desc: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] has sent a list of arms: #v 10#! small arms to be transferred to us under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. The envoy has brought a draft treaty. It needs only our signature.
nesnd_external_request_arms_event_desc: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_external_requester').GetName] has sent an envoy to request #v 10#! small arms under a treaty binding for #v 1 year#!. The bill of lading is already on the foreign ministry's desk.
nesnd_external_accept_request: Very well. Draw up the treaty.
nesnd_external_refuse_request: We are stretched thin ourselves. We must decline.
nesnd_external_dismiss_desc: Fold up the letters of credence and withdraw any requests still awaiting an answer. Treaties already in force must be handled separately through diplomacy.
nesnd_external_resume_desc: The Southern crisis is not over; our envoys can set out again. Aid already agreed in the last round cannot be negotiated a second time.
nesnd_external_end_desc: The Southern succession has been decided, and our envoys have come home to report. The treaties we signed still stand. Every payment and every shipment of arms they promise must still be delivered.
nesnd_external_end_no_partner_desc: There is no one left to receive our letters, and the envoy has come home. Treaties already signed will still be honoured.
